findings.title: Ceiling command omits unheld provider-job spend
findings.description: `ceiling_values` sets the 30-day cap from `planned + trailing`, but the estimate’s `trailing_30d_usd` excludes unheld provider jobs. The purchase guard includes those jobs in its 30-day total, and the estimate exposes them separately in `unheld_jobs` (`src/manta_trading/data/tick/purchase_plan.py:296-299`). When unheld jobs exist, the printed command can therefore set a cap too low for the guard to allow the purchase. Include that spend in the suggested cap or stop with a message explaining the additional amount.

findings.title: Provider holes are exempted without checking the condition
findings.description: `_LISTED_NEVER` exempts every `provider_hole` session before checking its `condition`. The cutover design only exempts a provider hole on a `missing` day. A `provider_hole` status can also come from a unit whose fetch status is `PROVIDER_HOLE` (`src/manta_trading/data/tick/tick_status.py:114-116`); if its condition is not missing, this code can omit an unaccounted session from the report and exit rule. Check the condition before treating the session as exempt.

findings.title: Any health exit-code change fails, including changes the cutover allows
findings.description: `final_failures` unconditionally adds a failure when the health exit differs from the baseline. The 307 design explicitly permits a health change caused by an `over` or failed unit when that change is named in the evidence. With this unconditional comparison, those documented, accounted-for cases still prevent the cutover from passing. Apply the stated exception when evaluating the health change.
